teaches: A story from history: the archive is the material, each part marked as history and told with its date; open on the moment it went wrong; every part a problem and its answer; land on the image that closes it.

packet.title: Apollo 13: the explosion
sentences: Fifty-five hours into the flight, an oxygen tank on Apollo 13 exploded about two hundred thousand miles from Earth.
The tank fed the command module, Odyssey, the only part of the spacecraft with a heat shield.
Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert and Fred Haise powered Odyssey down and moved into the lunar module, Aquarius.

packet.title: Living in the lander
sentences: Aquarius was designed to keep two people alive for about two days and had to keep three alive for four.
Carbon dioxide built up because the lander's filters were nearly spent.
The command module's spare filters were square and the lander's slots were round.
Engineers in Houston designed a fix from plastic bags, cardboard, suit hoses and duct tape and read it up by radio.
The crew swung around the Moon and used its gravity to head back toward Earth.
Mission control was flooded with calls from the public.

packet.title: Splashdown
sentences: On the last morning the crew powered Odyssey back up and released Aquarius.
Odyssey splashed down in the Pacific on the seventeenth of April.
